articles/commands.html.title: Commands | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/commands.html.summary: Commands Command Action /me text Action, shown as * you text /plain text Send without Markdown formatting /join #room:server Join a room by alias, room ID or link; see Joining rooms /leave Leave the current room /topic text Set the topic /invite @user:server Invite a user /name text Set the room name /avatar [file] Set the room avatar from an image; /avatar none removes it /kick @user:server [reason] Remove a member /ban @user:server [reason] Remove a member and stop them joining again /unban @user:server Let a banned user back /power @user:server level Set a power level: a number, or admin, moderator or member /op @user:server, /deop @user:server Make a member admin, or an ordinary member /msg @user:server Start a direct chat /nick name Set your display name /list [server] Browse the public rooms of your server, or of another server /create name Create a private room /create #room [name] Create a public room with the address #room:yourserver, listed in the room directory /alias #room, /unalias #room Add or remove an address of the current room /publish, /unpublish List the current room in your server's public room directory, or remove it /upload Send a file /devices Manage your sessions /settings View and change options /logs Read this and earlier session logs /call Voice call the other member of this direct chat /answer Answer the ringing call /reject Decline the ringing call /hangup End the call, or cancel one that rings /mute Mute or unmute your microphone in the call /audiotest Hear yourself a second later, through the Opus codec of calls, to test the microphone and speaker; close the dialog to stop /encryption Show encryption, recovery and backup state /recover Unlock older messages with the recovery key /verify [@user:server] Verify this device with your other devices, or a user, with emoji /ignore [@user:server] Block a user: their messages and invites no longer show; without a user, list whom you block /unignore @user:server Unblock a user /report [@user:server] Report a user, or without one this room, to your server's admins /whois [@user:server] A user's devices and the addresses they last connected from; yours without admin rights /accounts [text], /rooms [text] Server admins: list and manage the server's accounts or rooms; see Server administration /suspend @user:server, /unsuspend @user:server Server admins: let the user read but not send, join or invite; or end it /lock @user:server, /unlock @user:server Server admins: refuse the account's sessions until unlocked /notice @user:server text Server admins: send a server notice /tokens, /reports Server admins: registration tokens, and users' reports /quit Exit

articles/encryption.html.title: Encryption and devices | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/encryption.html.summary: Encryption and devices Encryption Messages in encrypted rooms are encrypted on your device before they leave it, and only the devices of the people in the room can read them; the server only sees ciphertext. New private rooms and direct chats are encrypted from the start, and encryption cannot be turned off for a room again. The recovery key lets a new sign-in prove it is you and read messages from before it existed. Setting up recovery creates three things: cross-signing keys, which vouch for your devices; a backup of message keys on the server, encrypted so the server cannot read it; and the recovery key itself, which is shown once. Write it down or copy it somewhere safe. If you set up recovery in another app, such as Element, use that app's recovery key or passphrase. Verification compares seven emoji on two devices to prove that no one is in between. Both devices must show the same emoji in the same order; if they differ, cancel, and nothing is trusted. A device you verified receives the cross-signing and backup keys, so it does not need the recovery key. You can also verify other people, so you know their devices are really theirs. In the terminal client, the room's frame shows [encrypted]. Room → Enable encryption turns it on for an existing room. File → Encryption shows this device's ID and fingerprint, and whether cross-signing, key backup and the recovery key are set up. Other clients, such as Element, list the same fingerprint for this session. A message that arrived before its key shows [encrypted message; the key has not arrived] and is decrypted as soon as the key comes. Your other verified devices are asked for missing keys automatically. Files sent to encrypted rooms are encrypted too; previews and Save file decrypt them on this device. If encryption is not available on this computer, messages to encrypted rooms are not sent; they are shown in red with the reason, so nothing is ever sent unencrypted by mistake. Recovery key and key backup Set up recovery (File → Encryption) is offered only when your account has no cross-signing yet. The server may ask for your password. While a backup is on, new room keys are uploaded to it. Recover (File → Encryption, or /recover) on a new sign-in asks for the recovery key, or the passphrase if you set one in another client. It verifies this device, restores the key backup and decrypts the stored messages that were waiting for keys. Verifying devices File → Verify this device (or /verify) asks your other devices to verify this one: accept on a device that is already trusted and compare the emoji. Verify selected in File → Devices verifies the device you pick. /verify @user:server verifies another person. When someone asks to verify you from their app, such as Element, in your direct chat, the request shows there as a message and the client asks you to accept it. File → Devices marks devices that your current identity has not signed as Not trusted, on red. Only a trusted device can vouch for another, so verify an untrusted device with a trusted one, or use your recovery key. Accept on the other device. When both show the same emoji, choose They match on both; if they differ, choose They don't match. File → Devices shows each device as verified, cross-signed (verified through your cross-signing keys) or unverified. Room keys and secrets are shared only with your verified or cross-signed devices. Devices File → Devices (or /devices) lists your sessions with their last activity; this one is marked *. You can rename a device, or log out one or all other devices, which asks for your password. To end this session, use File → Log out.

articles/files.html.title: Files and images | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/files.html.summary: Files and images Files Room → Send file (or /upload) opens a file browser; the file is uploaded and sent as an image, video, audio or file message. You can also drag files onto the terminal window, or paste their paths: when the input line holds nothing but paths of existing files, Enter asks whether to send them, and No puts the text back to edit. Attachments show as [image: cat.png, 120 KB]. The Save file action asks where to save, starting with a free name in your downloads folder; give a file, or a folder to save into. The folder is Ui:DownloadDirectory, or ~/Downloads when it is unset; with Ui:AskWhereToSave off, files are saved there without asking. Images Images in the log get a preview under the message, drawn with shade blocks: 20:01 <alice> [image: ring.png, 1 KB] ░▒▓▓█████▓▓▒░ ░▓██▓▒░ ░▒▓██▓░ ▓██░ ░██▓ ▓██░ ░██▓ ░▓██▓▒░ ░▒▓██▓░ ░▒▓▓█████▓▓▒░ The preview grows with the window: by default it uses the full width of the message log and up to three quarters of its height, and it is redrawn when you resize the terminal. It is made from an 800×600 thumbnail, so it loads quickly. The View image action opens the full image: terminals that support the Kitty or Sixel graphics protocols (kitty, WezTerm, foot, Konsole, recent xterm) show real pixels; others show colored blocks. PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP and TGA are supported; other formats such as WebP show [no preview] and can still be saved. Previews are set in appsettings.json: "Ui": { "InlineImages": true, "ImagePreviewColumns": 0, "ImagePreviewRows": 0, "ImagePreviewStyle": "Blocks", "DarkBackground": true } Setting Meaning StartRoom Room ID or alias to open at start; the first room when unset InlineImages false turns previews off ImagePreviewColumns, ImagePreviewRows Largest preview in cells; 0 follows the window ImagePreviewStyle Blocks ( ░▒▓█, dithered), Ascii (70 characters from . to @$) or Braille (2×4 dots per cell, the most detail) DarkBackground false on a light terminal, so dark parts of the image are drawn

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Requirements A terminal with UTF-8 and colors: GNOME Terminal, Konsole, kitty, xterm, tmux, Windows Terminal, macOS Terminal An account on a Matrix homeserver, for example @alice:matrix.org Install See Installing: with apt on Debian and Ubuntu, from the release archives on Windows and other Linux systems, or from source. Run Start the client; on Windows, run Uniform.Chat.exe: ./Uniform.Matrix Double-clicking Uniform.Chat in a file manager works too: on Linux it opens itself in a terminal window, the desktop's default terminal or the one in the TERMINAL environment variable. The first time, it asks for your full Matrix user ID, such as @alice:matrix.org. Give the server address too only when the server cannot be found from the user ID, for example http://localhost:8008 for a server of your own on this computer. Then it asks for your password and logs in. After a successful login it saves the user ID and address to your settings, and remembers the session, so later runs start straight away without asking. You can also give them on the command line, which skips the question: --Matrix:UserId=@alice:matrix.org, and --Matrix:Homeserver=http://localhost:8008 when needed. Without a terminal to ask in, for example with input redirected, the client prints this help instead. Messages are kept in a local database under ~/.local/share/uniform-chat-terminal/, and messages you write are kept there until the server has received them, so nothing is lost when the connection drops. The window has a menu bar, a room list, the messages of the selected room and its members. Type a message and press Enter to send it; see Interface for menus, keys and /commands. Settings can be changed in File → Settings, which saves them to ~/.config/uniform-chat-terminal/settings.json; see Settings, which also lists every command-line parameter. They can also go in appsettings.json next to the program, for example "Matrix": { "UserId": "@alice:matrix.org" }. Command-line options override both. Each run writes its own log under ~/.local/share/uniform-chat-terminal/logs/; View → Logs shows them. To log out on the server, choose File → Log out. Quitting with Ctrl+Q keeps the session. Create an account On the first start, give the user ID you want, such as @alice:example.org, where the part after : is the server, and choose Create account. The client asks for a password twice, then for what the server needs: a registration token from the server's admin, and acceptance of its policies, shown with their addresses. It then creates the account and logs in. Many servers do not let apps create accounts: then make the account on the server's website and log in here. Delete the account File → Delete account… asks you to confirm, then for your password. You leave every room, your name and picture are removed, and every device is signed out. The account cannot be used again, and nobody can take its user ID. The client then quits and forgets the user ID. Troubleshooting Message Meaning M_FORBIDDEN: Invalid username or password Wrong user ID or password. No valid m.homeserver.base_url for ... The server's discovery file is broken; contact its administrator. M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED ... (retry after N s) The server limits logins; wait N seconds.

articles/install.html.title: Installing | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/install.html.summary: Installing The client runs on Linux and Windows, on x64 and arm64 processors. It brings everything it needs; no .NET or other runtime has to be installed. Apt install On Debian and Ubuntu, x64 and arm64, install from the apt repository of Uniform Chat, which is kept in its releases on GitHub. Add the repository once, with the key its packages are signed with: sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings curl -fsSL https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/latest/download/uniform-chat-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg > /dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg] https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/ latest/download/" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/uniform-chat.list sudo apt update Then install the client: sudo apt install uniform-chat-terminal Start it with the command uniform-chat-terminal. sudo apt upgrade updates it with the rest of the system. sudo apt remove uniform-chat-terminal removes it, but not your account and messages in ~/.local/share/uniform-chat-terminal. From the release archives Download uniform-chat-terminal-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz (or linux-arm64, or win-x64.zip and win-arm64.zip for Windows) from the releases and unpack it anywhere. The program is Uniform.Chat, or Uniform.Chat.exe on Windows. The docs folder in it has this guide; open docs/index.html in a browser. From source Install the .NET 10 SDK and run dotnet build in the repository root; then use dotnet run --project src/Uniform.Chat.Terminal -- in place of the program in this guide.

articles/interface.html.title: Interface | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/interface.html.summary: Interface File Room View Help ┌Rooms─────────────────┐┌General — Welcome to the general chat────────────┐┌Members (3)──────┐ │ 1 General (2) ││12:01 <alice> hi all ││alice │ │ 2 @bob ││12:02 <bob> hello! this is a long message that ││bob │ │ 3 +Secret project ││ wraps under the text ││carol │ │ ││12:02 -!- carol joined ││ │ │ ││12:03 * alice waves ││ │ │ ││12:04 <you> on my way [sending…] ││ │ └──────────────────────┘└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘└─────────────────┘ hello everyone_ F1 Help │ Ctrl+N Rooms │ Ctrl+O Join │ Ctrl+Q Quit │ Connected as @you:matrix.org bob typing… Menu bar (F10 or the mouse) has everything the client can do: File, Room, View and Help. Help → About shows the client's version. Rooms lists invites (+), favourites, other rooms and low-priority rooms. Direct chats are marked @. The number is the Alt key for the room; unread counts are in brackets, and rooms that mention you are yellow. Message log shows the selected room, with its name and topic in the frame. Long lines wrap under the text, own messages are cyan, and messages still being sent say [sending…]. A day change is marked with a line. Members lists who is in the room, admins (@) and moderators (%) first, as in irssi; invited users are marked +. F2 hides it. Input line sends what you type to the room. Lines starting with / are commands. Status bar shows key hints, the connection state and who is typing. Others see when you are typing too. Messages you write are stored first and sent in order, so they survive a lost connection or a restart. If the server refuses one, for example because you left the room, it is shown in red with the reason. Menus Menu Items File Encryption, Verify this device, Devices, Settings, Log out, Quit Room Join, Room directory, New room, New public room, Direct message, Send file, Invite, Set topic, Set name, Set avatar, Add alias, Directory listing, Power level, Kick, Ban, Unban, Enable encryption, Leave View Older messages, Members, Select message, Logs, Audio test, Next room, Previous room Help Commands and keys, About Keys Key Action Alt+1 … Alt+9 Go to room 1–9 Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P Next, previous room Up, Down in the room list Look through rooms; focus stays in the list (click the list, or press Tab on an empty input line, to get there) Enter in the room list Type in the selected room; for an invite, join or reject it PageUp, PageDown Scroll messages Ctrl+PageUp Load older messages Ctrl+O Join a room Ctrl+R Room directory, also of other servers F1 Help F2 Show or hide members Ctrl+Up, Enter Select a message and act on it Tab Complete a member's name; at the start of the line it adds : Esc Cancel a reply or edit; leave the message log F10 Open the menu Ctrl+Q Quit

articles/joining.html.title: Joining rooms | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/joining.html.summary: Joining rooms Rooms can be on any Matrix server; your server joins them for you. You can join a room by its alias, its room ID or a link, find it in a room directory, or follow a link in a message. By alias, ID or link Press Ctrl+O, or type /join followed by the room: You give Example An alias /join #matrix:matrix.org A room ID /join !abc123:example.org A link /join https://matrix.to/#/#matrix:matrix.org or /join matrix:r/matrix:matrix.org Links can carry the servers to join through, as ?via= in a matrix.to link. You can also give the servers after the room yourself: /join !abc123 matrix.org example.org Rooms of newer versions have IDs without a server, like !abc123; joining them needs at least one server that is in the room. Aliases don't need servers, as the alias's server tells where the room is. A room you are already in opens instead. Room directory Press Ctrl+R, or type /list, to browse the public rooms of your server. Type a search in Search and press Enter. To browse another server, type its name in Server, e.g. matrix.org, and press Enter; /list matrix.org opens the directory on that server directly. Leave Server empty for your own. The directory remembers the last server until you quit. Choosing Join joins the selected room through the server that listed it. Links in messages Select a message with Ctrl+Up and press Enter. Open link follows its room or user link: a room you are in opens, and other rooms are offered to join. A user link opens your direct chat with them, or offers to start one. See Acting on messages.

articles/messages.html.title: Messages | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/messages.html.summary: Messages Formatting Type Markdown and it is sent formatted, so other clients such as Element show bold, links and code: You type Others see **bold**, _italic_, ~~strike~~ bold, italic, strike `code` code [the spec](https://spec.matrix.org) a link named "the spec" https://example.org a clickable link Names completed with Tab become mentions, which notify that person. HTML you type is shown as text, not run as markup. Start a line with /plain to send it exactly as typed. Formatted messages from others are shown as text: *bold*, _italic_, ~strike~, `code`, • list items, > quotes, code blocks as they are, links as name (address), mentions by display name, and spoilers as [spoiler]. Acting on messages Press Ctrl+Up to select the newest message, move with the arrow keys, and press Enter for its actions: Action Key What it does Reply R The input line shows [re nick]; your next message is a reply. Esc cancels. React A Pick a common emoji or type your own reaction. Edit E Your own messages only. The text moves to the input line, [edit] is shown; Enter saves, Esc cancels. View image V Images only. Opens the full image in a viewer. Save file S Attachments only. Downloads the file to ~/Downloads. Open link L Messages with room or user links, such as https://matrix.to/#/#room:server. Opens a room you are in or a direct chat you have, or offers to join the room or start a chat. With several links, pick one. Delete D Your own messages only, after confirmation. Deletes it for everyone. Report P Others' messages. Sends a report, with the reason you pick, to the admins of your server. Block sender B Others' messages. Hides the sender's messages and invites, as /ignore does. Esc returns to the input line. Replies show what they answer, like <bob> [re alice: lunch at noon?] sure. Reporting and blocking Report messages, people and rooms that break the rules: spam, harassment, sexual or violent content, or anything illegal. Reports go to the admins of your server; the person reported is not told. Report a message from its actions, a person with /report @user:server, and the open room with /report. /ignore @user:server blocks someone: their messages and invites no longer show, on all your devices, and they are not told. /ignore alone lists whom you block, and /unignore @user:server shows their new messages again.

articles/rooms.html.title: Room administration | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/rooms.html.summary: Room administration Admins and moderators can change the room and its members from the Room menu or with commands; the server refuses what your power level does not allow. Set name, Set topic and Set avatar (an image file; /avatar none removes it). Kick removes a member, who may join again; Ban also stops them joining again, and Unban lets them back. A reason is optional. Power level makes a member an admin (100), a moderator (50) or an ordinary member (0), or gives any level. Lowering your own level asks first, as you cannot raise it back yourself. Members can be given by user ID or, when it is unique in the room, by display name. Public rooms and addresses A public room is one anyone can join, also from other servers. Room → New public room, or /create #room Room name, creates one with the address #room:yourserver and lists it in your server's room directory. Public rooms are not encrypted, as anyone can join and read them. Add alias, or /alias #room, gives the current room another address on your server. The first address becomes the room's main address, which other clients show. /unalias #room removes an address. Directory listing, or /publish and /unpublish, lists the room in your server's public room directory, or removes it. Listing does not change who may join; the room's join rule decides that. Addresses can only be made on your own server. People on other servers find listed rooms with their client's room directory by choosing your server; see Joining rooms.

articles/server-admin.html.title: Server administration | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/server-admin.html.summary: Server administration If you are an admin of your homeserver, the Server menu manages the server remotely: its accounts, registration tokens, reports and rooms. The client uses the admin API that Synapse defined, which Uniform Chat Server also has. For others, the server refuses with "You are not a server admin." Accounts, or /accounts [text], lists the accounts whose user ID or name contains the text, with their devices, rooms and flags: admin, suspended, locked, deactivated. + New account creates one with a password. Choose an account to: see its devices and the addresses they last connected from (Who is, also /whois @user); send it a server notice; reset its password, which logs out its devices; suspend it, or end the suspension; lock it, or unlock it; make it a server admin, or take the rights away; deactivate it for good. Registration tokens, or /tokens, lists the tokens new accounts register with, with how often each was used and when it expires. Choose + New token to create one: give its text or leave it empty for a random one, then how many accounts may use it and for how many days. Choose a token to delete it. Reports, or /reports, lists what users reported, newest first. Choose a report to delete it, suspend the reported user, or shut the room down. Rooms, or /rooms [text], lists the server's rooms, most members first. Choose a room to see its members or shut it down. Server notice, or /notice @user text, sends a message from the server. It arrives in the user's own Server notices room, where only the server writes. Who is works for anyone on their own account. You cannot suspend, lock, deactivate or take admin rights from your own account, so you cannot shut yourself out. Suspend and lock Suspended: the user can still read, leave rooms and log out, but cannot send messages, join or create rooms, invite, change their profile or upload files. Use it while you look into a report. Locked: the server refuses every request of the account until you unlock it. Its devices stay signed in and continue once it is unlocked; this client shows "Retrying: The account is locked by an admin." meanwhile. /suspend @user and /unsuspend @user, /lock @user and /unlock @user do the same from the message line. Shutting down a room Shutting a room down makes every member from your server leave and forget it, and deletes its addresses on your server; the reason you give is shown to them. Shut down and block also keeps your server's users from joining it again. Members from other servers stay in the room, and its messages stay on your server.

articles/settings.html.title: Settings | Uniform Chat Terminal
articles/settings.html.summary: Settings Settings come from these places; later ones override earlier ones: appsettings.json next to the program ~/.config/uniform-chat-terminal/settings.json (under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set), written by the settings window Environment variables, with __ between parts: Matrix__UserId=@alice:matrix.org The command line: --Matrix:UserId=@alice:matrix.org Changes applied in the settings window, until the client exits Application parameters Every setting can be given on the command line as --Section:Name=value. The ones you need at the start: ./Uniform.Chat --Matrix:UserId=@alice:matrix.org --Matrix:Password=secret Matrix:UserId is your full Matrix ID, such as @alice:matrix.org. It is needed at every start, as it chooses your local data; save it in the settings file to start without options. Without one, the client asks for it in the window. Matrix:Password is used only for the first login. When it is not given, the client asks for it, which keeps it out of your shell history. Matrix:Homeserver is the server address, for servers that cannot be found from the user ID. --help lists every parameter with its default. All of them: Parameter Default Meaning Matrix:UserId not set Your full Matrix ID, e.g. @alice:matrix.org. Needed at every start; save it in the settings file. Matrix:Password not set Password for the first login; asked for when not given. Not needed once you are logged in. Matrix:Homeserver not set Server address, when it cannot be found from the user ID, e.g. http://localhost:8008 for a server on this computer. Matrix:DeviceName Uniform Chat Terminal Display name of the device created at login. Matrix:SyncTimeout 00:00:30 Long-poll time of each sync request. Matrix:RequestTimeout 00:05:00 How long to wait for the server to answer a request; joining a large room on another server can take minutes. Matrix:TimelineLimit 50 Timeline events per room in each sync. Matrix:OutboxRetryInterval 00:00:15 Wait before retrying unsent messages after a transient failure. Storage:DataDirectory not set Root directory; when unset, the application's data directory, e.g. ~/.local/share/uniform-chat-terminal. Storage:DatabaseFileName client.db Database file name inside each account directory. Storage:MediaDirectoryName media Media cache directory name inside each account directory. Storage:LogDirectoryName logs Directory inside DataDirectory with one log file per session. Storage:LogFilesKept 20 Session log files to keep; older ones are deleted at start. Ui:StartRoom not set Room ID or alias to open at start; the first room in the list when null. Ui:InlineImages true Whether to show ASCII previews of images in the message log. Ui:ImagePreviewColumns 0 Widest preview in terminal columns; 0 fills the width of the message log. Ui:ImagePreviewRows 0 Tallest preview in terminal rows; 0 allows three quarters of the message log's height. Ui:ImagePreviewStyle Blocks Drawing style: Blocks shades, Ascii characters or Braille dots. Ui:DarkBackground true Whether the terminal background is dark, so bright pixels get dense characters. Ui:DownloadDirectory not set Folder that saved files go to; when null, ~/Downloads if it exists, otherwise the home folder. Ui:AskWhereToSave true Whether Save file asks where to save, starting from DownloadDirectory; otherwise files are saved there under a free name. Audio:Microphone not set Microphone: an ALSA device name on Linux, e.g. pulse, or part of the device's name on Windows; the system's default when null. The audio test lists the choices. Audio:Speaker not set Speaker: an ALSA device name on Linux, or part of the device's name on Windows; the system's default when null. The audio test lists the choices. Logging:LogLevel:Default Information Lowest level written to the log for categories without their own setting. Settings window File → Settings (or /settings) lists every option with its current value, where the value comes from, and a description of the selected option. Edit (or Enter) changes the selected option; options with fixed values, such as yes/no or the image preview style, offer a list. Apply uses the changes now, until the client exits. Options marked ↻ take effect only after a restart. Save writes the changes to ~/.config/uniform-chat-terminal/settings.json (under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set), which is read at every start. Reset undoes one step at a time: first an edit that is not applied, then an applied change that is not saved. Pressed again, it removes the option from the settings file on save, so the default applies again. Load reads another settings file as changes to apply or save; Export writes the current settings to a file. Edited options are marked *, applied but unsaved ones +. Values given on the command line override the settings file; the source column shows command line for them. The password is never shown or saved. Logs View → Logs (or /logs) shows the log of this run and earlier ones; each run writes its own file, and the oldest beyond Storage:LogFilesKept are deleted. Pick a run on the left. Level cycles the lowest level shown, Alt+F focuses the text filter, and Enter shows a whole entry, such as an error with its stack trace. Warnings are yellow and errors red; the current run's log follows new lines while scrolled to the end.

index.html.title: Terminal Client | Uniform Chat Terminal
index.html.summary: Uniform Chat Terminal A chat client for Matrix, the open chat protocol, that runs in a text terminal: menus, a room list, the message log and members, an input line for messages and irssi-style /commands, and a status bar. It supports end-to-end encrypted rooms and files, key backup with a recovery key, and emoji verification of devices. Messages you write are kept on your computer until the server has them, so nothing is lost when the connection drops. Note The client is in early development. Installing: with apt on Debian and Ubuntu, or from the release archives. Getting started: run and log in. Interface: the window, menus and keys. Messages: formatting, replies, edits, reactions and more. Files and images: sending, saving and image previews. Encryption and devices: recovery key, key backup and verification. Room administration: names, avatars, kicks, bans and power levels. Commands: the /commands of the input line. Settings: command-line parameters, the settings file and logs. There is also a graphical app for Windows, Linux and Android; see its guide. To run a homeserver of your own, see the server guide.
